differences.title: 1. INITIAL LOAD
differences.leftDesc: Renders on server, sends HTML. Reduces client JS.
differences.rightDesc: Sends HTML and JS. Hydration needed.

differences.title: 2. DATA FETCHING
differences.leftDesc: Fetch data directly on the server before sending.
differences.rightDesc: Requires separate API calls from the client.

differences.title: 3. INTERACTIVITY
differences.leftDesc: Can't directly use client-side hooks or event listeners.
differences.rightDesc: Full access to browser APIs and events.

differences.title: 4. BUNDLE SIZE
differences.leftDesc: Less JavaScript sent to the client.
differences.rightDesc: More JavaScript needed for client-side logic and hydration.

differences.title: 5. SEARCH ENGINE OPTIM.
differences.leftDesc: Fully rendered HTML is easily crawlable by search engines.
differences.rightDesc: Relies on crawlers executing JavaScript effectively.

differences.title: 6. ACCESS TO APIS
differences.leftDesc: Can directly use server-side Node.js modules and APIs.
differences.rightDesc: Limited to browser global objects and APIs.

differences.title: 7. CODE EXECUTION
differences.leftDesc: Code runs on the server, reducing client processing.
differences.rightDesc: Code runs in the user's browser.
